title: Detecting and Mitigating Subliminal Bias Transmission in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
summary: This paper proposes a framework to detect and mitigate subliminal bias transmission in multi-agent LLM systems. By analyzing hidden statistical dependencies in synthetic data generated by biased teacher models, we introduce a modular filtering mechanism that identifies and neutralizes biased patterns without requiring explicit bias labeling. The approach combines mechanistic interpretability techniques with adversarial training to isolate and suppress neuron populations responsible for transmitting biases. Validation involves measuring bias amplification rates across generations of student models trained on synthetic datasets, comparing outcomes against baseline systems lacking mitigation.
gap: Existing multi-agent LLM frameworks like FACET lack mechanisms to detect or neutralize biases transmitted through synthetic data, assuming teacher models are unbiased or that biases remain static.
approach: We implement a three-stage pipeline: (1) mechanistic analysis to identify bias-correlated neuron populations, (2) adversarial filtering to generate bias-neutral synthetic data, and (3) curriculum learning to train student models on progressively debiased datasets. The system incorporates real-time bias monitoring through controlled continuation tasks.
evaluation: We evaluate using political bias metrics on generational datasets, comparing bias amplification rates against baseline systems. Additional metrics include task performance retention and neuron activation pattern divergence between biased and mitigated models. Baselines include unmodified multi-agent systems and post-hoc debiasing methods.
